It was played by 12 teams. The national champion was [[Club Universitario de Deportes|Universitario]].[https://universitario.pe/noticias/historia/1999-un-bicampeonato-inolvidable 1999: un bicampeonato inolvidable][https://www.americatv.com.pe/deportes/futbol-peruano/universitario-deportes-recordo-titulo-1999-conseguido-estadio-matute-n441143 Universitario de Deportes recordó título de 1999 conseguido en el estadio de Matute][https://www.rsssf.org/tablesp/peru99.html Rsssf.org Peru 1999] The national championship was divided into two half-year tournaments, the [[Apertura and Clausura|Torneo Apertura]] and the [[Apertura and Clausura|Torneo Clausura]]. Each was played on a home-and-away [[Round-robin tournament|round-robin]] basis. The winners of each would play for the national title in a playoff. If the same club had won both tournaments, it would have won the national championship automatically. Following-season [[Copa Libertadores]] berths went to the champion, as well as to the best other team in the aggregate table. The bottom team on the aggregate table was relegated, while the eleventh place held a promotion play-off against the winner of the Segunda División (Second Division). == Teams == ===Team changes=== {| class="wikitable" |- !
